## Research 1 of 3: the shape model

Code read on `origin/main` (2026-11-22). Context pack: `.claude/tmp/context/3351.md`. I read these ranges myself again: `crates/sim/src/verify/swept.rs:1-18`, `crates/sim/src/verify/probe.rs:97-110` and `:175-290`, `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:40-90`, `crates/app/src/operation/tool_law.rs:1-160`, `crates/tools/src/spun.rs:1-60`, and the tool doors in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (`:1184`, `:1378`, `:1476`, `:1575`, `:1661`, `:1763`, `:1867`, `:1964`, `:2032`, `:2301`).

### What the code does today

- The tool shape is the closed enum `ToolKind` (23 kinds, `crates/tools/src/tools.rs:24-137`) and the flat `Tool` struct (one `diameter`, `corner_r`, `tip_angle`, `flute_len`, shank and holder fields). A tip form is a kind, not a parameter.
- `Taper` is a sharp cone. It reads only `tip_angle`. #895 (not shipped) adds a tip diameter and a tip form.
- The project file already has a general outline: `ToolDto::cutter` (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs:465-471`, `[z, r, arc]` for each point, tip up). Its type is `SpunProfile` (`crates/tools/src/spun.rs`): up to 64 points, each segment a line or a circular arc with a signed radius. Today only the editor, the side view and the neck bands read it. No generator, no stock simulation and no gouge law reads its tip.
- The verifier already judges a tool as a UNION of atoms (`probe.rs:180-230`). Each atom is a convex solid of revolution with a concave radius profile `rho(z)` (`swept.rs:1-18`). The atom kinds are `Flat`, `Bull`, `Cone`, `Dove` and `Ball` (`probe.rs:241`). The swept law is exact for each convex atom (golden-section search on a convex function).
- `section::tangency` (`section.rs:82`) reads one radius, `cx.tool.radius`, for the wall law.
- The 2D and 3D kernels read one number, `tool_diameter * 0.5`. The 3D finish and the multi-axis family refuse every kind except `BallNose` at their doors.

### The geometry fact that decides the model

Any meridian made of lines and arcs splits into convex atoms:

- A straight segment is a frustum. A frustum is convex for each slope: up (chamfer bit, V-groove, tapered flank) and down (dovetail, the existing `Dove`).
- An arc that bulges away from the axis (ball tip, bull corner, the bead of an ogee) is a torus zone with concave `rho(z)`. It is convex. The existing `Bull` and `Ball` atoms are two cases of it.
- An arc that bulges toward the axis (the cutting arc of a roundover bit, the cove part of an ogee) is not convex. Chord frusta cover it: each chord lies outside the arc, so the union is a little larger than the tool (an outer bound). The tangent polygon gives an inner bound. The sag of each chord is `R (1 - cos(theta / 2))` for an arc step `theta`, so a sag limit gives the number of chords. `SpunProfile` already flattens arcs by this rule (`spun.rs:9-14`).

A union of convex solids is exact for each law that takes the worst atom: the swept penetration, the drop-cutter height (the highest contact of all atoms), and the dexel and field cuts (the union of the cuts). An outer bound can only over-report a gouge or lift a drop-cutter point. It can never hide a cut. The inner bound is the bound for rest material, so a later operation never assumes that material is gone when it is not.

### The options

| Option | What it is |
|---|---|
| A. More closed kinds | One `ToolKind` and new fields for each shape: `TaperedBall`, `TaperedFlat`, `Roundover`, `Cove`, `ChamferBit`, `VGroove`, `Ogee`. |
| B. One general profile | Each tool is a meridian `rho(z)` (lines and arcs). The named kinds become presets that write a meridian. |
| C. Hybrid (recommended) | The named kinds stay as they are, with their fields and file words. Each kind gives its meridian through one function. New shapes come from two places: the tip form on `Taper` (#895) and one new kind `FormMill` whose meridian is the stored `cutter` outline. Every consumer reads only the meridian and its convex atoms. |

### Cost of each option in each consumer

| Consumer | A. Closed kinds | B. One profile | C. Hybrid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool file and migration | A new word and fields for each kind in `ToolDto`, `ToolKindDto`, `Def`, `KindWord`. Additive, no version step. | Every tool writes a profile. Each old file must convert on load. This is a breaking file change and a migration for each old kind. | `Taper` gets the additive #895 fields. `FormMill` gets one additive word, `form_mill`, and uses the `cutter` field that exists. No migration, no version step (the additive rule of `file.rs`, as #894 did). |
| Tool dialog | One page of fields for each kind (7 new pages). | One outline editor for all tools. The user loses the simple number fields. | The number fields stay. `Taper` gets a tip form row. `FormMill` gets a preset list (roundover, cove, chamfer bit, V-groove, ogee) with its numbers, and the Profile tab (`tool_cutter_page.rs`) for a drawn outline. |
| 2D compensation radius at a depth | A new branch for each kind in each kernel. | One law: the radius `rho(z)` at the contact height. | The same one law as B, on the meridian. |
| 3D drop-cutter and surface offset | A closed form for each kind (vertex, edge and facet contact). | One law: the drop height of the union is the highest drop height of its atoms. Each atom type (flat disc, frustum, torus zone) needs its contact formulas one time. | The same as B. |
| Stock simulation (column and field) | A new dexel atom and a new `SdfTool` variant for each kind. | One revolved atom of the meridian, split into convex pieces. | The same as B. The existing variants stay until a test proves each one equal to its meridian. |
| Verifier and gouge/collision atoms (convexity law) | A new `Prof` for each kind. The roundover arc breaks the convexity law and needs its own law. | Two new `Prof` kinds: a frustum (it replaces `Cone` and `Dove`) and a torus zone (it covers `Bull` and `Ball`). Concave arcs become chord frusta. The convexity law of `swept.rs` stays as it is. | The same as B. |
| Holder and shank checks | No change. `ToolGeom` reads `diameter`. | No change for the stack bands. A pilot bearing is a non-cutting band. | The same as B. |
| Post tool table | A table word for each kind. | One "form" word for all tools. The controller loses the ball and bull words. | The old kinds keep their words. `FormMill` posts a form word and its preset name. The compensation radius is the radius at the contact height, or the post refuses control compensation. |

### Recommendation: option C, the hybrid

- It is the only option without a file migration. Old projects and the starter catalogue load unchanged, and the old kinds keep their posts and tool tables.
- All consumers get one plug-in point: `Tool::meridian()` and its convex atoms. Each consumer does the work one time, not once for each shape (the cost of A).
- The convexity law of the verifier stays true. Only the atoms change. The proof of `swept.rs` (Boyd and Vandenberghe 3.2.5, Kiefer 1953) stays valid. No new search method is necessary.
- The outline storage exists (`ToolDto::cutter`, `SpunProfile`). Its arc sign and its conservative flattening are already the rules that the atoms need.
- Option B is dropped: it breaks every saved tool and removes the simple fields that users know from tool catalogues. Option A is dropped: seven shapes times nine consumers, and each new router bit is a new kind.

### How the existing issues fit

- #895 (taper tip diameter, tip radius, tip form): folded in. Its research is the specification of the `Taper` tip form. The sub-issues of this umbrella do its slices.
- #896 (form and undercut cutters): the sub-issues here do its corner-rounding part with `FormMill`. The undercut forms (back-chamfer, slitting saw) and their operations stay in #896.
- #1974 (lollipop in 5-axis finishing): kept as it is. The lollipop head is already a convex `Ball` atom (#1444). Its work is multi-axis reach and neck avoidance, not the shape model.
- #1893 (3D Deburr with a lollipop): kept as it is. It stays blocked on #896.

### Sources (public only; no text copied)

- Tool geometry terms (cutting diameter, angle per side, tip diameter, tip radius, roundover radius, pilot bearing diameter, cutting height): the public catalogues of end mill and router bit makers, and the cutter geometry chapters of Machinery's Handbook.
- Drop-cutter for general cutters: Yau, Chuang and Lee, "Numerical control machining of triangulated sculptured surfaces in a stereo lithography format with a generalized cutter", Int. J. Production Research 42(13), 2004, pp. 2573-2598. Hwang and Chang, "Three-axis machining of compound surfaces using flat and filleted endmills", Computer-Aided Design 30(8), 1998, pp. 641-647.
- Convexity and the search: Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, section 3.2.5. Kiefer 1953 (golden-section search). `swept.rs` already names these sources.
- Chord and tangent polygons of an arc: elementary plane geometry (sagitta), as `spun.rs` already uses.
- Our own code, as listed at the top. No HSMWorks material.

## Research 2 of 3: the operation kinds and the new shapes

Source: the family sets in `crates/app/src/operation/tool_law.rs` (read on `origin/main`), the `tool_kinds:` rows of `kinds.rs`, and the shape doors in `generate.rs`. The new shapes are:

- tapered flat end mill and tapered ball nose: `Taper` with the tip form `Flat` or `Ball` (#895);
- chamfer bit: `Taper` with tip form `Flat` (sharp or flat tip), with an optional pilot band;
- V-groove bit: `Taper` (sharp, as today) or `Taper` with a small tip radius;
- roundover (corner-rounding), cove, ogee and other router form bits: `FormMill` with a preset meridian.

### The laws for the new shapes

- **2D compensation at a depth.** For a vertical wall, the cutter centre offset is the LARGEST radius `rho(z)` of the meridian in the height band where the cutter overlaps the wall. This is conservative: no part of the tool enters the wall. For a cylinder it is `diameter / 2`, so the value for the old kinds does not change.
- **Edge form law (new).** A form bit cuts an edge, not a wall. The user gives the edge and the form depth. The cutter axis rides at the offset `rho(z_low)` from the wall, where `z_low` is the lowest height of the form band. The tip height puts the top of the form band on the top face. For a roundover of radius `R` with a pilot radius `r_p`: offset `r_p`, tip at `top - R` (below the pilot band, if one is present). The cut declares an `EdgeBreak` of the form shape, so `credit_breaks` and `deviate` read the rounded edge as intended. This is the corner-rounding law of #896 Q3, made general for any meridian.
- **Pilot bearing.** A bearing does not cut. It is a non-cutting band of the meridian. It must clear the wall by the gouge tolerance. Contact of a bearing with the part is a collision. On a CNC machine the path guides the tool, so the bearing is not needed.
- **Cutter compensation in the control.** The controller applies one radius from its table. For a `FormMill` and a tip-formed `Taper`, that radius is not `diameter / 2`. The post refuses `Control` compensation for these tools by name. `Wear` compensation stays: the path is the centre path, and the control adds only the wear delta.
- **V-Carve depth.** The depth at a local half-width `w` is the inverse of the meridian: the height where `rho(z) = w`. For a sharp cone this is the law of today. For a flat or ball tip, it is the same law on the real tip.

### The table

The new edge form law. An `EdgeBreak` of a circular and of a general form. |
| Deburr | `CONE`: `Taper` | `Taper` with each tip form | `FormMill`: the edge dihedral angle does not match a form. | #895 slice 4 (real-tip offset along the edge normal sum). |

### Rules that each sub-issue keeps

- Each new shape stays refused at every door until the verifier and both stock simulation engines read its meridian. A door opens only in the sub-issue that proves the toolpath for it.
- The test `no_orphan_tool_kinds` (`crates/app/tests/tool_law.rs`) needs one operation for each kind. `FormMill` is in the 2D Chamfer family from its first sub-issue. Its generator door refuses it by name until the edge form sub-issue opens it.
- The old kinds keep identical toolpaths, stamps, digests and stock simulation results. Each consumer sub-issue pins this.

Each sub-issue is `enhancement`, `P4`, `source:agent`, and quotes the words of the maintainer. Each one is linked as a sub-issue of this issue.

Follow-up outside the plan: #3376 (`P8`): tapered tools in Swarf, the 5-axis family and 3D Pocket. Until then those kinds refuse the new tools by name.

The fit of the existing issues (comments posted on each, labels not changed):

- #895: folded in (#3368, #3370, #3371, #3373).
- #896: the corner-rounding part is in #3369, #3370, #3371 and #3375. The undercut forms stay in #896.
- #1974 and #1893: kept as they are.

Decisions taken without the maintainer:

- The hybrid model, not more closed kinds and not one profile for all tools (Research 1 has the reasons).
- The edge form law goes in 2D Chamfer, not in 2D Contour: 2D Chamfer already places the tool from the edge and declares the `EdgeBreak`.
- No project-file version step: each new field and the word `form_mill` are additive (the rule in `file.rs`, as #894 did). The body of this issue named a version bump; it is not necessary.

This issue closes now, so that Pick takes only the sub-issues for code.
Research done; the sub-issues #3367 to #3375 carry the work (dependency order in the comment above). Claim released.
